title: Existence of one regular affine descent of an ordinary resolution rule
statement:
Fix a totally ordered label type $L$. Let $A$ be a rule on reduced finite-type rational schemes admitting a closed embedding in a smooth separated finite-type rational scheme [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data, def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule, def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. It assigns finite ordinary blowup towers with distinct increasing labels, coherent ideals with nonempty nowhere dense regular centers, and regular final scheme; its empty-input tower has length zero. For each open immersion of embeddable inputs over the rational base, its specified label-preserving cartesian contraction comparison deletes exactly the stages whose extended ideals are unit ideals [def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map, def-nagata-extended-ideal, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme].

Assume padded overlap compatibility: the three full restrictions of the assigned coproduct tower along three open lifts of any affine overlap have one common labeled ordinary realization contracting to the assigned overlap tower [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data]. For every reduced finite-type rational input $S$, there exists a labeled ordinary tower $B$ on $S$ which is a resolution (regular nonempty nowhere dense centers, coherent center ideals, regular last level and every level finite type over the rational base), and is an affine descent of $A$: some finite affine cover of $S$ has embeddable coproduct total $T$ and a full cartesian comparison $A(T)\to B$ preserving all labels and actual extended ideals [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data]. No compatibility between different covers is asserted.

proof.text: First check the domains of the constructions. The field $\mathbf Q$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $\mathbf Q$), so $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open subscheme of $S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. In particular an open immersion into $S$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image over any affine open of $S$ is another open subscheme of $S$. It is therefore of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and its source is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The same reasoning applies to affine opens inside intersections. Since $S$ is quasi-compact, [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] gives a finite affine cover, including the empty cover when $S$ is empty.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4--2.1.9, 2.2.11, 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.5(ii), printed pp.87--88,91--92; explicit labeled Zariski-descent expansion.

proof.text: Each affine open $V$ used here is reduced by the local-ring definition [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] its coordinate algebra is generated by finitely many elements over $\mathbf Q$. Sending variables to these generators presents it as $\mathbf Q[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/K$. Thus [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives a closed embedding $V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_{\mathbf Q}$. This ambient scheme is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], and of finite type by its polynomial coordinates. Consequently every such $V$ belongs to $\mathcal C$, and so do the finite disjoint unions of charts, by the stipulated closure of $\mathcal C$. In particular $A(U)$ and every $A(W)$ on an affine overlap are defined.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4--2.1.9, 2.2.11, 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.5(ii), printed pp.87--88,91--92; explicit labeled Zariski-descent expansion.

proof.text: Use the assumed padded overlap compatibility to identify the full chart towers and their actual ideals on all affine double and triple refinements. All original labels are retained. This supplies the overlap identifications used in the following sectionwise ideal descent.

Here is the ideal descent at a fixed label, with no ideal-gluing assertion left implicit. Suppose the current scheme $S_i$ has already been constructed with its open cover $S_{i,a}=S_i\times_SU_a$ identified with the corresponding levels of $T|_{U_a}$. Let $I_{i,a}$ be the local ideal at $\lambda_i$. Step 4 identifies these ideals on overlaps. For any open $V\subset S_i$ set
$$I_i(V)=\{s\in\mathcal O_{S_i}(V):s|_{V\cap S_{i,a}}\in I_{i,a}(V\cap S_{i,a})\text{ for every }a\}.$$
The sheaf condition of $\mathcal O_{S_i}$ and of each $I_{i,a}$ proves that this is a sheaf of ideals. On $S_{i,a}$ the condition for $a$ implies all the others, by overlap equality, so $I_i|_{S_{i,a}}=I_{i,a}$. It is unique with these restrictions because sheaf membership is local. It is quasi-coherent and of finite type by the neighborhood definitions in [pqf-def-coherent]. It is coherent as well: for a map from a finite free sheaf on any open, its kernel restricts on this cover to the corresponding kernel for the coherent local ideal, and finite type of that kernel is the same neighborhood condition. This argument also covers a unit ideal on some of the charts.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4--2.1.9, 2.2.11, 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.5(ii), printed pp.87--88,91--92; explicit labeled Zariski-descent expansion.

proof.text: Start the induction with $S_0=S$ and the given opens $U_a$. Having descended $I_i$ as in Step 5, define $S_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i}(S_i)$ using [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Step 3 and [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] identify its restriction over $S_{i,a}$ with the next level of $T|_{U_a}$, with its center and transition map. These are compatible on overlaps by Step 4 and [prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent]. The inverse images of the $S_{i,a}$ form an open cover of $S_{i+1}$, so the induction continues for all $n$ labels. Its pullback to the disjoint union $U$ is exactly $T$, with no deleted stage. At each stage the blowup is proper by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper], because $I_i$ is of finite type. Proper includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; composing with the finite-type structure morphism of $S_i$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] proves that $S_{i+1}$ remains of finite type over $\mathbf Q$. This constructs the required tower for this cover.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4--2.1.9, 2.2.11, 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.5(ii), printed pp.87--88,91--92; explicit labeled Zariski-descent expansion.

proof.text: The descended center $V(I_i)$ restricts on $S_{i,a}$ to the open part of the center of $T$ over the $a$th component. Since these opens together are all of the corresponding level of $T$, nonemptiness of its center shows $V(I_i)\ne\varnothing$. If $V(I_i)$ contained a nonempty open in $S_i$, intersecting it with a chart meeting it would give nonempty interior in the corresponding local center, contrary to the nowhere-dense center of $T$. Thus the descended center is nowhere dense. Its open pieces are regular, since they are open subschemes of the regular center of $T$; the local rings agree under open restriction. The same argument applies to the last level: its covering opens are open parts of the regular last level of $T$. The local-ring characterization in [def-weil-regular-scheme] proves regularity of the center and of $S_n$. Empty chart pieces cause no problem, since regularity there is vacuous.

proof.text:
finite type over the Noetherian field Q makes S Noetherian and quasi-compact.
Choose a finite affine open cover; for empty S choose the empty cover. Each chart
and every affine open in an intersection is reduced and finite type over Q, since
opens in a Noetherian scheme are quasi-compact and open immersions are locally of
finite type. Its coordinate algebra has finitely many generators, giving a closed
embedding in affine space. This ambient is smooth, separated and finite type.
Finite disjoint unions of these presentations show that the coproduct T of the
charts is an embeddable rational input. Use its actual coproduct maps to obtain a
ResolutionAffineCover, and let its assigned tower have length n and its given labels.
Retain all n stages on each chart. The padded-overlap hypothesis identifies their
full ideals and blowups on affine refinements of every double and triple overlap.
Induct on those n labels, starting with S. At a given level, define its ideal on an
open V to consist of sections whose restrictions to every lifted chart belong to
that chart's center ideal. Overlap equality shows that this restricts to the given
ideal on each chart. The sheaf condition proves that it is an ideal sheaf and that
it is unique with those restrictions. Quasi-coherence and finite type are local.
For coherence, the kernel of any map from a finite free module restricts to the
finite-type kernel for each coherent chart ideal; these local generators prove
finite type of the kernel, including on charts with unit ideal. Blow up that ideal.
Flat base change along the lifted open charts identifies the next level with their
next assigned levels, preserving all transitions and centers; uniqueness of blowup
lifts proves agreement on refinements. Continue to the last label, producing the
full cartesian map to A(T) without contraction. Every center is nonempty because
its pullback to T is; it has empty interior because any nonempty open in its support
would meet a chart in a nonempty open of the local center. Its local rings are
regular because its chart pieces are open pieces of the regular center on T.
The same local-ring argument proves regularity of the last level. Properness of
finite-type blowups and finite-type composition give finite type of every level
over Q. Thus the resulting tower is a resolution and is an affine descent. With
the empty cover, A(T) has length zero, and the induction constructs the trivial tower.

theorem exists_affine_resolution_descent {L : Type w} [LinearOrder L]
    (A : OrdinaryZariskiResolutionRule.{u, w} L) (_hpad : A.HasPaddedOverlaps)
    (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) :
    ∃ B : LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme, B.IsResolution ∧ A.IsAffineDescent S B
